prompt: Education is not a luxury, but a basic human right and as such should be free for everyone irrespective of personal wealth. Do you agree or disagree?
essay:
In recent years, education has been treated as if it is a luxury rather than a basic human right, despite being vital for everyone regardless of their financial situation. I totally agree with the view that education should not be associated with wealth. This essay will discuss the benefits of providing free education as well as some of the disadvantages it may cause.

One major benefit of free education is that individuals from poor countries will have the opportunity to acquire advanced knowledge. Many students from different parts of the world have ambitious goals and aim for a brighter future; however, their financial situation can prevent them from pursuing higher education. This is because they may have to choose between spending their limited money on essential needs and paying for their education. Therefore, providing free access to advanced educational resources and tutoring sessions can give these individuals the opportunity to develop their knowledge and achieve their goals.

On the other hand, free education may also create some disadvantages, particularly a lack of resources. If numerous individuals are able to pursue education without worrying about the cost, schools and universities may struggle to accommodate the increasing number of students. For example, educational institutions may experience overcrowded classrooms and a shortage of teachers and learning materials. As a result, the quality of education could decrease because there may not be enough resources to meet every student’s needs.

In conclusion, although free education can provide individuals from less wealthy backgrounds with valuable opportunities, it can also put pressure on educational resources. Therefore, I believe that education should be accessible to everyone, but certain limitations may be necessary to ensure that sufficient resources are available for all students.
